text.headline: Timeline of Latvia
text.text: Major events in the history of Latvia.

events.headline: Earliest Settlements
events.text: The territory of modern Latvia has been inhabited since the Neolithic period, with evidence of early settlements dating back to around 3000 BC.

events.headline: Foundation of Riga
events.text: Riga, the capital of Latvia, was founded by German bishop Albert of Buxhoeveden, marking the beginning of significant German influence in the region.

events.headline: Riga Joins the Hanseatic League
events.text: Riga became a member of the Hanseatic League, a powerful economic alliance of trading cities in Northern Europe, enhancing its trade and influence.

events.headline: Livonian War
events.text: The Livonian War began, leading to the division of Livonia between Sweden and Poland-Lithuania, significantly impacting Latvia's territorial and political landscape.

events.headline: Swedish Rule Established
events.text: Following the Treaty of Altmark, Sweden gained control over much of Latvia, initiating a period of Swedish rule that lasted until the Great Northern War.

events.headline: Russian Empire Takes Control
events.text: The Great Northern War resulted in the defeat of Sweden, and Latvia came under the control of the Russian Empire, marking a new era in its history.

events.headline: Emancipation of Serfs
events.text: The serfs in Latvia were emancipated, leading to significant social and economic changes in the region as peasants gained more rights.

events.headline: 1905 Revolution
events.text: The 1905 Revolution in Russia sparked widespread unrest in Latvia, leading to demands for greater autonomy and rights for the Latvian people.

events.headline: Declaration of Independence
events.text: Latvia declared its independence from Russia, establishing itself as a sovereign nation after World War I.

events.headline: Peace Treaty with Soviet Russia
events.text: The Treaty of Tartu was signed, recognizing Latvia's independence and establishing its borders with Soviet Russia.

events.headline: Soviet Occupation
events.text: Latvia was occupied by the Soviet Union as part of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, leading to significant political repression and loss of sovereignty.

events.headline: Nazi Occupation
events.text: During World War II, Latvia was occupied by Nazi Germany, resulting in severe persecution of the Jewish population and other groups.

events.headline: Return to Soviet Control
events.text: As World War II ended, Latvia was reoccupied by the Soviet Union, leading to further repression and the imposition of Soviet policies.

events.headline: Chernobyl Disaster
events.text: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster had significant health and environmental impacts on Latvia, contributing to growing anti-Soviet sentiments.

events.headline: Baltic Way
events.text: Over two million people joined hands to form a human chain across the Baltic States, including Latvia, in a peaceful protest for independence from Soviet rule.

events.headline: Restoration of Independence
events.text: The Supreme Council of Latvia declared the restoration of independence from the Soviet Union, marking a pivotal moment in Latvian history.

events.headline: Soviet Union Acknowledges Independence
events.text: Following the failed coup in Moscow, Latvia's independence was recognized by the Soviet Union, solidifying its status as a sovereign state.

events.headline: NATO and EU Membership
events.text: Latvia joined NATO and the European Union, marking a significant step in its integration into Western political and security structures.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: The COVID-19 pandemic affected Latvia significantly, leading to health crises and economic challenges, as well as a national response to manage the situation.

events.headline: Support for Ukraine
events.text: In response to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Latvia has actively supported Ukraine, providing military aid and welcoming refugees.
